newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end down on banks' selloff.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end down on banks' selloff.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Monday, reflecting banks' efforts to liquidate excess funds at the end of a reserve period, but dealers expected a rebound on Tuesday at the start of the new reserve period.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.335 percent against Saturday's 5.538 close, with commercial paper down to 5.25-5.50 percent from 5.50 percent.
Dealers said market liquidity likely would tighten on Tuesday's scheduled maturation of T$30 billion in central bank repurchase agreements.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.1200-1300 percent against 6.0600-0625 and the 10-year 84/1 bond yield was at 5.9400 against 5.8550.
